senses.title: Relating to building design: the professional core
senses.titleCN: 与建筑设计有关：职业核心义
senses.definition: relating to the art and practice of designing buildings, recorded from 1759
senses.definitionCN: 与设计建筑的艺术和实践有关，此义记录于 1759 年
senses.example: The competition rewarded architectural design rather than engineering cost.
senses.exampleCN: 竞赛看重的是建筑设计，而不是工程造价。
senses.why: Architectural is architecture + -al, and architecture is the art of building. The suffix turns the discipline into an adjective, so the first sense names whatever belongs to the designer's art.
senses.whyCN: architectural 是 architecture + -al，而 architecture 是建筑的艺术。后缀把学科变成形容词，因此第一义指属于设计者技艺的一切。

senses.title: Of a building: built according to design principles
senses.titleCN: 建筑物的：按建筑原理建造的
senses.definition: of a structure, built or judged according to the principles of architecture, a sense recorded from the 1610s for architecture itself
senses.definitionCN: 指建筑物按建筑原理建造或评价，该义在 1610s 已见于 architecture
senses.example: The shed is useful but has no architectural quality at all.
senses.exampleCN: 这间棚屋很实用，却毫无建筑品质。
senses.why: The adjective transfers from the art to its product. A building is architectural when it can be judged by the art's rules, not merely when it stands up.
senses.whyCN: 形容词从“艺术”转移到“产物”。一座建筑之所以是 architectural，是因为能用建筑学的规则来评判它，而不只是因为它立得住。

senses.title: Of a style or period: Gothic, Baroque, modern
senses.titleCN: 风格或时期的：哥特式、巴洛克式、现代式
senses.definition: characteristic of a particular period, movement or regional building tradition
senses.definitionCN: 具有某一时期、流派或地区建筑传统特征的
senses.example: The church is Victorian Gothic, a purely architectural label.
senses.exampleCN: 这座教堂是维多利亚哥特式，这是一个纯建筑学的标签。
senses.why: Styles are the grammar of the art. Once buildings are classified by pointed arches or concrete slabs, 'architectural' comes to mean 'belonging to that grammar' rather than to any single building.
senses.whyCN: 风格是建筑艺术的语法。一旦建筑按尖拱或混凝土板被分类，architectural 就表示“属于那套语法”，而不是属于某一座建筑。

senses.title: Of drawings and models: the design on paper
senses.titleCN: 图纸与模型的：纸上的设计
senses.definition: relating to drawings, models or plans that specify how a building is to be made
senses.definitionCN: 与规定建筑如何建造的图纸、模型或方案有关
senses.example: The architectural drawings show a stair that the model omits.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑图纸上画了一部楼梯，模型里却漏掉了。
senses.why: The design exists before the building. Paper and card carry the art in advance, so the adjective attaches to the instruments that translate intention into construction.
senses.whyCN: 设计先于建筑存在。纸张和卡纸提前承载了这门艺术，因此形容词也附着于把意图转成施工的那些工具。

senses.title: Figurative framework: the architecture of an institution
senses.titleCN: 比喻性框架：制度的结构
senses.definition: relating to the underlying structural framework of an organisation, law or system, not to physical buildings
senses.definitionCN: 与组织、法律或系统的底层结构框架有关，而非物理建筑
senses.example: The constitutional settlement has an architectural logic that the reforms ignored.
senses.exampleCN: 宪制安排有一套建筑式的逻辑，而改革忽视了它。
senses.why: A building is a frame that carries loads; an institution is a frame that carries rights and duties. The same structural image lets architectural describe any carefully designed framework.
senses.whyCN: 建筑是承重的框架；制度是承载权利与义务的框架。同一幅结构意象让 architectural 可以形容任何精心设计的框架。

senses.title: Computing: the architecture of hardware and software
senses.titleCN: 计算机：硬件与软件的体系结构
senses.definition: relating to the layered design of a computer system, its instruction set or its software structure
senses.definitionCN: 与计算机系统的分层设计、指令集或软件结构有关
senses.example: An architectural flaw let one process read another's memory.
senses.exampleCN: 一个体系结构缺陷让一个进程能读取另一个进程的内存。
senses.why: Computer design borrowed the builder's word: processors, caches and layers are arranged like floors and load-bearing walls. Architectural therefore marks the plan rather than the code.
senses.whyCN: 计算机设计借用了建造者的词：处理器、缓存与层次像楼层和承重墙一样被安排。因此 architectural 标记的是“设计图”，而不是代码本身。

senses.title: Landscape architecture: designed outdoor space
senses.titleCN: 景观建筑：被设计的室外空间
senses.definition: relating to the planned arrangement of gardens, parks and outdoor spaces
senses.definitionCN: 与花园、公园及室外空间的规划布局有关
senses.example: The garden's architectural planting frames the view rather than filling it.
senses.exampleCN: 花园里建筑式的种植框住了景致，而不是填满它。
senses.why: Landscape architecture treats plants, paths and walls as building elements. Architectural here means that outdoor space is composed with the same structure, scale and rhythm as a facade.
senses.whyCN: 景观建筑把植物、路径和墙当作建筑元素。这里的 architectural 意为室外空间以与立面相同的结构、尺度与节奏被组织起来。

senses.title: Photography: buildings as the subject
senses.definition: describing photographs that treat buildings, their lines and volumes as the main subject
senses.definitionCN: 指以建筑、其线条与体量为主要题材的照片
senses.example: Her architectural photographs flatten a cathedral into geometry.
senses.exampleCN: 她的建筑摄影把一座大教堂压平成几何图形。
senses.why: If the art is the subject, the photograph that studies it is architectural. The adjective moves from the object to the way the object is pictured.
senses.whyCN: 如果这门艺术是题材，研究它的照片也就是 architectural。形容词从对象转移到对象的观看方式。

senses.title: Heritage: buildings protected as evidence
senses.titleCN: 遗产：作为证据受保护的建筑
senses.definition: relating to buildings and structures valued and protected for their historical or aesthetic significance
senses.definitionCN: 与因历史或美学价值而受珍视和保护的建筑与构筑物有关
senses.example: The whole district was listed as architectural heritage.
senses.exampleCN: 整个街区被列为建筑遗产。
senses.why: When a building is valued as evidence of an art and a period, protection attaches to its architectural character. The adjective then names what the law and the museum preserve.
senses.whyCN: 当一座建筑作为某门艺术与某个时期的证据而被珍视，保护就附着于它的建筑特征。形容词于是命名法律与博物馆所保存的东西。

senses.title: Architectural acoustics: sound shaped by a space
senses.titleCN: 建筑声学：被空间塑造的声音
senses.definition: relating to the behaviour of sound in a designed room or building
senses.definitionCN: 与声音在被设计的房间或建筑中的行为有关
senses.example: The hall's architectural acoustics favour a string quartet over a lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 这座大厅的建筑声学更适合弦乐四重奏，而不是讲座。
senses.why: A building does not only carry loads; it also carries sound. Once surfaces and volumes are designed as part of the art, architectural extends to how a space sounds.
senses.whyCN: 建筑不只承重，也承载声音。一旦表面与体量被当作艺术的一部分来设计，architectural 就延伸到“空间听起来如何”。

intro.en: Architectural is a transparent derivative: architecture + -al, recorded in 1759. The whole family runs back through Latin architectura to Greek arkhitekton, 'chief builder', where arkhi- means chief and tekton means builder. That arkhi- is not the archaeo- of archaeology.
intro.cn: architectural 是透明的派生词：architecture + -al，记录于 1759 年。整个词族经由拉丁语 architectura 追到希腊语 arkhitekton“首席建造者”，其中 arkhi- 意为首席，tekton 意为建造者。这个 arkhi- 不是 archaeology 的 archaeo-。

items.en: Architecture enters English in the 1560s as 'the art of building', from French architecture and Latin architectura. Architect follows in the same decade from French architecte.
items.cn: architecture 于 1560 年代以“建筑的艺术”进入英语，来自法语 architecture 和拉丁语 architectura。architect 也在同一时期从法语 architecte 进入。

items.en: Latin architectus goes back to Greek arkhitekton 'master builder, director of works', a compound of arkhi- 'chief' (related to archon 'ruler') and tekton 'builder, carpenter'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 architectus 可追到希腊语 arkhitekton“首席建造者、工程主管”，由 arkhi-“首席”（与 archon“统治者”相关）和 tekton“建造者、木匠”复合而成。

items.en: By the 1610s architecture also names the building itself as something built according to architectural principles, not only the art.
items.cn: 到 1610 年代，architecture 也指按建筑原理建造的建筑物本身，而不再只指这门艺术。

items.en: Architectural is first recorded in 1759 as architecture + -al, the Latin adjective suffix -alis. It makes the discipline usable as a modifier.
items.cn: architectural 于 1759 年首次记录，由 architecture + -al（拉丁形容词后缀 -alis）构成。它使这门学科可以作为修饰语使用。

items.en: The arkhi- of architect means 'chief'; the archaeo- of archaeology means 'ancient'. They are different Greek stems and the two families are unrelated in meaning.
items.cn: architect 的 arkhi- 意为“首席”；archaeology 的 archaeo- 意为“古老”。它们是不同的希腊词干，两个词族在意义上并无关联。

items.en: From the 20c architectural extends to computing, landscape design, photography and heritage law, always keeping the idea of a designed frame.
items.cn: 20 世纪以后，architectural 扩展到计算机、景观设计、摄影与遗产法，始终保留“被设计的框架”这一观念。

note.en: The first group separates the base words from a dangerous look-alike with a different Greek stem; the second separates adjectives that also describe structure.
note.cn: 第一组区分基础词与一个词干不同的危险形似词；第二组区分同样描述结构的形容词。

entries.definition: The person who designs buildings. Architectural is the adjective from the abstract noun architecture, not from this person noun.
entries.definitionCN: 设计建筑的人。architectural 来自抽象名词 architecture，而不是这个指人的名词。

entries.definition: The art of building, or the buildings produced by it. Add -al to this noun to get architectural.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑的艺术，或由此产生的建筑。给这个名词加 -al 就得到 architectural。

entries.definition: Relating to archaeology. It shares the arch- look but comes from arkhaios 'ancient', not from arkhi- 'chief'.
entries.definitionCN: 与考古学有关的。它同样以 arch- 开头，但来自 arkhaios“古老”，不是 arkhi-“首席”。

entries.definition: Relating to the load-bearing frame or to the arrangement of parts. It stresses how something holds together, while architectural stresses design.
entries.definitionCN: 与承重框架或部件安排有关。它强调事物如何支撑，而 architectural 强调设计。

entries.definition: Relating to the process of constructing rather than to the finished design.
entries.definitionCN: 与建造过程有关，而不是与完成后的设计有关。

entries.definition: Relating to architecture as a system, or to a unified organising structure in art or thought. It is more technical than architectural.
entries.definitionCN: 与作为体系的建筑术有关，或与艺术、思想中的统一组织结构有关。它比 architectural 更技术化。

normalIntro.en: The links are real: architecture + -al, the Greek arkhi- 'chief' plus tekton 'builder', and the contrast with archaeological.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想是真实的：architecture + -al，希腊语 arkhi-“首席”加 tekton“建造者”，以及与 archaeological 的对照。

normal.en: architecture + -al = architectural. The noun names the art; the adjective describes anything that belongs to it.
normal.cn: architecture + -al = architectural。名词命名艺术，形容词描述属于这门艺术的一切。

normal.en: architect = arkhi- 'chief' + tekton 'builder': a chief builder, not an old builder. That separates it from archaeology.
normal.cn: architect = arkhi-“首席”+ tekton“建造者”：首席建造者，不是古老的建造者。这条就把它与 archaeology 分开。

normal.en: The four everyday frames are architectural design, style, history and drawings.
normal.cn: 四个日常搭配是 architectural design、style、history 与 drawings。

normal.en: The figurative branch keeps the image of a frame: constitutions and software both have architecture before they have walls.
normal.cn: 比喻分支保留“框架”意象：宪法与软件都先有 architecture，才有“墙”。

normal.en: In a city, architectural quality is what survives the estate agent's description: proportion, structure and detail.
normal.cn: 在城市里，architectural 品质就是房产广告词褪去后仍留下的东西：比例、结构与细部。

abstract.en: Draw a floor plan over a photograph: the same building exists twice, once as design and once as mass.
abstract.cn: 在照片上叠一张平面图：同一座建筑存在两次，一次作为设计，一次作为体量。

abstract.en: Think of a skeleton inside a body: architectural is the frame that lets the surface stand.
abstract.cn: 想象身体里的骨架：architectural 就是让表面得以站立的框架。

abstract.en: The word always points to intention: something architectural was arranged by someone, not merely piled up.
abstract.cn: 这个词始终指向意图：被称为 architectural 的东西是被人安排过的，而不只是堆起来的。

examples.en: The museum's architectural value lies in its concrete shell, not its exhibits.
examples.cn: 这座博物馆的建筑价值在于它的混凝土外壳，而不在展品。

examples.en: They hired a photographer to record the architectural details before restoration.
examples.cn: 他们请了一位摄影师在修复前记录建筑细部。

examples.en: The software has an architectural problem that no patch can fix.
examples.cn: 这个软件有一个任何补丁都修不好的体系结构问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿基泰克扯罗」——阿基泰克在桌上扯罗蓝图，一笔画出拱门和梁柱 → architectural 建筑的、建筑设计的

root: 由 architecture + -al（拉丁 -alis）构成，1759 年首次记录；architecture 出自拉丁 architectura，再往前是希腊 arkhitekton“首席建造者”= arkhi-“首席”+ tekton“建造者”。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of architectural all describe something arranged by design: a profession, a building judged by its art, a style, a drawing, a constitutional frame, a computer system, a garden, a photograph, protected heritage, and the sound of a room.
sensesIntro.cn: architectural 的十个义项都在描述“被设计安排之物”：职业、按艺术标准评判的建筑、风格、图纸、宪制框架、计算机系统、花园、照片、受保护的遗产，以及一个房间的声音。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blueprint weighted by a ruler, lines becoming arches, columns and beams.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张用尺压住的蓝图，线条变成拱、柱与梁。

branches.en: THE DESIGN CORE: the profession and its drawings, where the building exists before it is built.
branches.cn: 设计核心：职业与其图纸，建筑在建成之前已存在于此。

branches.en: THE BUILT RESULT: a structure judged by architectural rules, and a style that classifies it.
branches.cn: 建成结果：按建筑规则评判的构筑物，以及对它进行分类的风格。

branches.en: FRAMES WITHOUT WALLS: institutions and computer systems inherit the builder's structural image.
branches.cn: 没有墙的框架：制度与计算机系统继承了建造者的结构意象。

branches.en: OUTDOOR AND PICTURED: gardens composed like facades, and buildings turned into photographs.
branches.cn: 室外与影像：像立面一样构图的园林，以及被拍成照片的建筑。

branches.en: PROTECTED AND PERFORMED: heritage status preserves a building's character, and acoustics shows that character is also heard.
branches.cn: 保护与体验：遗产身份保存建筑的特征，声学则表明这种特征也能被听见。

intro.en: Architectural stacks three layers: Greek arkhi- 'chief' + tekton 'builder' gave arkhitekton, Latin made architectus and architectura, French passed architecture to English, and English added the adjective suffix -al in 1759.
intro.cn: architectural 叠了三层：希腊语 arkhi-“首席”+ tekton“建造者”给出 arkhitekton，拉丁语造出 architectus 与 architectura，法语把 architecture 传给英语，英语又在 1759 年加上形容词后缀 -al。

latinIntro.en: Latin architectus and architectura are borrowings from Greek arkhitekton. The suffix -alis simply means 'pertaining to', and it is the same suffix seen in archival and archaeological.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 architectus 与 architectura 是借自希腊语 arkhitekton 的词。-alis 后缀只表示“与……有关”，它与 archival、archaeological 中的后缀相同。

senses.title: The structure of a system

senses.title: The preserved records: evidence kept on paper
senses.titleCN: 被保存的记录：留作证据的纸页
senses.definition: a collection of documents and records preserved because they serve as evidence of the past
senses.definitionCN: 因可作为过去之证据而被保存的文件与记录集合
senses.example: The archive contains every letter the company sent between 1900 and 1950.
senses.exampleCN: 这批档案包含了该公司 1900 至 1950 年间寄出的每一封信。
senses.why: Greek ta arkheia were public records kept by the city. The core image is a box of papers retained on purpose, so archive first names the records that are kept rather than thrown away.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 ta arkheia 是城邦保存的公共记录。核心意象是一只被有意留存而非丢弃的纸箱，因此 archive 首先指被保留下来的记录本身。

senses.title: The building: the place that holds the records
senses.titleCN: 建筑物：存放记录的场所
senses.definition: the room, building or institution where such records are stored and made available
senses.definitionCN: 存放这类记录并向人提供查阅的房间、建筑或机构
senses.example: The archive opens to researchers at nine in the morning.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆上午九点向研究者开放。
senses.why: The container for the records is named by the same word: arkheion was a public building, and the English noun can shift from papers to the roof that shelters them.
senses.whyCN: 保存记录的容器用同一个词命名：arkheion 本就是公共建筑，英语名词因此可以从纸张滑向庇护它们的屋顶。

senses.title: The data store: digital retention
senses.definition: a store of digital material kept for future use, backup or research
senses.definitionCN: 为将来使用、备份或研究而保存的数字资料库
senses.example: The server keeps an archive of every image uploaded since 2010.
senses.exampleCN: 服务器保存着自 2010 年以来上传的每一张图片的存档。
senses.why: The evidence no longer has to be paper. A folder of old files performs the same act of retention, so archive transfers to digital storage without changing its purpose.
senses.whyCN: 证据不必再是纸。一个装旧文件的文件夹执行同样的留存动作，因此 archive 不改其目的就转移到数字存储。

senses.title: The body of work: an artist's or studio's past output
senses.titleCN: 作品全集：艺术家或机构的过往产出
senses.definition: the accumulated past works of a person or organisation, kept as a record of their development
senses.definitionCN: 个人或机构积累的过往作品，作为其发展过程的记录
senses.example: The fashion house's archive supplied the prints for the new collection.
senses.exampleCN: 这家时装屋的档案库为新系列提供了印花图样。
senses.why: A studio's papers and samples are evidence of its own past. The word extends from public records to any accumulated body of work that can be consulted later.
senses.whyCN: 工作室的纸稿与样品是它自身过去的证据。这个词从公共记录扩展到任何可供日后查阅的累积作品。

senses.title: The compressed bundle: a file archive
senses.definition: in computing, a single file that bundles and often compresses many other files
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域，把许多文件打包、通常还压缩成的一个文件
senses.example: Download the .zip archive and unpack it into a new folder.
senses.exampleCN: 下载这个 .zip 压缩包，解压到一个新文件夹里。
senses.why: A physical archive box holds many papers in one container. The digital bundle reproduces that container, so the computing sense is a direct extension of 'many things kept together'.
senses.whyCN: 实体档案盒把许多纸张装进一个容器。数字压缩包复制了这个容器，因此计算机义是“许多东西被收在一起”的直接延伸。

senses.title: To file: enter a document into the collection
senses.definition: to file or enter a document into an archive collection, recorded as a verb from 1819
senses.definitionCN: 把文件归入档案集合，动词义记录于 1819 年
senses.example: The clerk archived the deed in the county record office.
senses.exampleCN: 职员把这份契据归入县档案室。
senses.why: Once the noun named the collection, the act of putting something into it became a verb. The box closes and the paper joins the row, so 'archive' means 'place into the kept set'.
senses.whyCN: 一旦名词命名了集合，把东西放进集合的动作就变成动词。盒子合上，纸页加入那一排，于是 archive 表示“放入被保存的集合”。

senses.title: To move data aside: long-term storage
senses.definition: to move digital material to a separate long-term store so that active systems stay uncluttered
senses.definitionCN: 把数字资料移到单独的长期存储中，使在用系统保持清爽
senses.example: The team archived last year's logs to free up the server.
senses.exampleCN: 团队把去年的日志存档，以腾出服务器空间。
senses.why: The verb keeps its filing meaning: material is moved from the active desk to the shelf. In computing the shelf is slower storage, but the action is still 'put away for later'.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留“归档”含义：材料从在用桌面移到架子上。在计算机里，架子是较慢的存储，但动作仍是“收起来备用”。

senses.title: To preserve for history: archive a website or a voice
senses.titleCN: 为历史保存：存档网站或口述
senses.definition: to capture and preserve something fragile or ephemeral so that later researchers can still consult it
senses.definitionCN: 抓取并保存易消失之物，使后来的研究者仍能查阅
senses.example: Librarians archived the protest website before it went offline.
senses.exampleCN: 抗议网站下线之前，图书馆员把它存档了。
senses.why: A website is a record that disappears when the server is switched off. Archiving it does what arkheia did for the city: it turns a live event into kept evidence.
senses.whyCN: 网站是记录，服务器一关就消失。给它存档，正是 arkheia 为城邦做过的事：把正在发生的事件变成被保存的证据。

senses.title: The personal store: memory as an archive
senses.titleCN: 个人储存：记忆作为档案
senses.definition: a figurative use for the accumulated store of memories, images or experiences that a person can draw on
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法：一个人可调用的记忆、影像或经验的累积储存
senses.example: Her childhood photographs are the archive of a vanished street.
senses.exampleCN: 她童年的照片就是一条消失街道的档案。
senses.why: Memory retains selected traces and can be searched later, exactly like a box of papers. The word moves from institutional records to the private store of experience.
senses.whyCN: 记忆保留经过挑选的痕迹，日后可被检索，完全像一箱纸。这个词从机构记录转移到私人的经验储存。

senses.title: The back issue: a journal's published past
senses.titleCN: 过刊：期刊已出版的过去
senses.definition: the collected back numbers of a newspaper or journal, available for consultation
senses.definitionCN: 报纸或期刊已出版的过刊合集，可供查阅
senses.example: The magazine's archive is searchable back to its first issue.
senses.exampleCN: 这份杂志的过刊可检索到创刊号。
senses.why: Each issue is a dated record, and together they form a run. The publishing archive is another shelf of the same strongroom, organized by date rather than by author.
senses.whyCN: 每一期都是有日期的记录，合起来形成一个序列。出版档案是同一间库房里的另一排架子，按日期而非按作者排列。

intro.en: Archive is a back-formation from archives, which entered English about 1600 from French archif and late Latin archivum. The source is Greek ta arkheia 'public records', kept in the arkheion or town hall, from arkhē 'government, beginning'. Although archaeology also goes back to arkhē, archive is not derived from archaeology.
intro.cn: archive 是由 archives 逆构而来的；archives 约于 1600 年从法语 archif 和晚期拉丁语 archivum 进入英语。其源头是希腊语 ta arkheia“公共记录”，保存在 arkheion（市政厅）中，出自 arkhē“政府、开端”。虽然 archaeology 也可追到 arkhē，但 archive 并不是由 archaeology 派生出来的。

items.en: Archives is first recorded about 1600 as 'records or documents preserved as evidence'. The plural is the original English form.
items.cn: archives 约于 1600 年首次记录，义为“作为证据保存的记录或文件”。复数形式才是英语最初的形式。

items.en: From French archif (16c.), which passed on the Latin word for written records and their repository.
items.cn: 来自法语 archif（16 世纪），后者把拉丁语中“书面记录及其存放处”的词传了过来。

items.en: Late Latin archivum, plural archiva, meant both 'written records' and the place where they were kept.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 archivum（复数 archiva）既指“书面记录”，也指存放这些记录的场所。

items.en: The source is Greek ta arkheia 'public records', the plural of arkheion 'town hall, public building', from arkhē 'government', literally 'beginning, origin, first place'. Arkhē is the verbal noun of arkhein 'to be the first'.
items.cn: 源头是希腊语 ta arkheia“公共记录”，即 arkheion“市政厅、公共建筑”的复数，出自 arkhē“政府”，字面为“开端、起源、首位”。arkhē 是 arkhein“居于首位”的动名词。

items.en: The singular archive is a back-formation from archives, made by treating the plural -s as a plural ending. The exact date is not fixed in the standard references and is best left uncertain.
items.cn: 单数 archive 是从 archives 逆构出来的：把复数的 -s 当成了复数词尾。通行资料未给出确切年代，此处如实存疑。

items.en: The verb is recorded in 1819 as 'to file or enter into an archive collection'. Digital and web senses follow in the late 20c.
items.cn: 动词义记录于 1819 年，意为“归档、纳入档案集合”。数字与网络义在 20 世纪晚期出现。

note.en: The first group separates the plural source and close derivatives from a false friend; the second separates places and things that store records.
note.cn: 第一组区分复数来源、近亲派生词与一个假朋友；第二组区分存放记录的场所与物件。

entries.definition: The original plural, meaning records or the institution that holds them. The singular archive was back-formed from it.
entries.definitionCN: 最初的复数形式，指档案或保管档案的机构。单数 archive 正是由它逆构而来。

entries.definition: A person who appraises, arranges and preserves archives. It is archive + -ist, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 负责鉴定、整理和保存档案的人。它是 archive + -ist，并非另一词根。

entries.definition: A curved structural opening, from Latin arcus 'bow'. It looks like the first syllable of archive but is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 拱形结构开口，来自拉丁语 arcus“弓”。它看起来像 archive 的第一音节，但并无词源关系。

entries.definition: A place where things are stored, especially records or objects. It stresses the container more than the historical evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 存放物品（尤指记录或器物）的场所。它比 archive 更强调容器，而非历史证据。

entries.definition: A single piece of written evidence. An archive is the organised collection of many records.
entries.definitionCN: 单份书面证据。archive 是许多 records 的有组织集合。

entries.definition: A secure room for valuables or records. It stresses protection from theft or damage, not public access.
entries.definitionCN: 存放贵重物品或记录的安全房间。它强调防盗防损，而非公共查阅。

normalIntro.en: The links are real: the Greek public records arkheia, the plural archives from which the singular was back-formed, and the 1819 verb.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想是真实的：希腊语公共记录 arkheia、逆构出单数的复数 archives，以及 1819 年的动词。

normal.en: Think of the plural first: archives are the records, and archive is the single collection or the act of filing.
normal.cn: 先记复数：archives 是记录，archive 是单数的集合或归档动作。

normal.en: Greek ta arkheia were public records kept in the town hall; the building and the papers share one name.
normal.cn: 希腊语 ta arkheia 是保存在市政厅的公共记录；建筑与纸张共用一个名称。

normal.en: A .zip archive is the digital version of a box: many files packed into one container.
normal.cn: zip 压缩包是盒子的数字版：许多文件被装进一个容器。

normal.en: The verb is 'put it in the box': archive a letter, archive a website, archive last year's logs.
normal.cn: 动词就是“放进盒子”：把信归档、把网站存档、把去年的日志归档。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with archaeology: archive goes back to arkhē 'government', not to arkhaios 'ancient'.
normal.cn: 别与 archaeology 混淆：archive 追到 arkhē“政府”，不是 arkhaios“古老”。

abstract.en: Picture a strongroom: the door closes, the date label is written, and a moment of the past is made reachable.
abstract.cn: 想象一间档案库：门关上，年份标签写好，过去的一刻变得可被触及。

abstract.en: The same act works on paper, film, code or memory: select, keep, label, and make searchable.
abstract.cn: 同一个动作作用于纸、胶片、代码或记忆：挑选、保留、贴标、使其可检索。

abstract.en: An archive is a promise that the future will still be able to ask questions of the past.
abstract.cn: 档案是一个承诺：未来仍然能够向过去提问。

examples.en: The letters lay in the archive for ninety years before anyone read them.
examples.cn: 这些信在档案馆里放了九十年，才有人读到。

examples.en: Please archive the signed contract under the client's name.
examples.cn: 请把签好的合同按客户姓名归档。

examples.en: The web archive kept a copy of the page after the site closed.
examples.cn: 网站关闭后，网络存档保留了这个页面的副本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿凯伍」——阿凯把五箱旧文件搬进库房，贴上标签锁好门 → archive 档案；归档

root: 由 archives 逆构而来；archives 约 1600 年借自法语 archif，源头为晚期拉丁 archivum 与希腊 ta arkheia“公共记录”（arkheion“市政厅”，出自 arkhē“政府、开端”）。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of archive all perform one act: select something, keep it, and make it consultable later. From papers and the building that holds them, the word extends to data, a body of work, a zip file, the act of filing, long-term storage, web preservation, memory, and back issues.
sensesIntro.cn: archive 的十个义项都在执行同一个动作：挑选某物、保存它、让日后可查阅。从纸张与保管它们的建筑，这个词扩展到数据、作品全集、压缩包、归档动作、长期存储、网络保存、记忆与过刊。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a labelled box of papers kept on purpose in a locked room.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只贴好标签的纸箱，被有意保存在上锁的房间里。

branches.en: PAPERS AND PLACE: the records and the building share one word, as arkheia and arkheion did.
branches.cn: 纸张与场所：记录与建筑共用一个词，正如 arkheia 与 arkheion。

branches.en: DIGITAL CONTAINERS: a data store and a zip bundle reproduce the box in another medium.
branches.cn: 数字容器：数据仓库与压缩包以另一种介质复制了这只盒子。

branches.en: ACCUMULATED OUTPUT: a studio's works and a journal's back issues are runs of dated records.
branches.cn: 累积产出：工作室作品与期刊过刊，都是按日期排列的记录序列。

branches.en: THE VERB: filing a document and moving data aside are the same 'put it away'.
branches.cn: 动词：归档文件与移走数据，都是同一个“收起来”。

branches.en: PRESERVING THE FLEETING: a website and a memory are saved so later questions can still be asked.
branches.cn: 保存易逝之物：网站与记忆被存下，使日后的提问仍能成立。

intro.en: Archive has no living prefix or suffix of its own: the word came whole from Latin archivum and Greek arkheion. English then built archival, archivist, archivable and archivism on the noun, and the plural archives is the historical source.
intro.cn: archive 本身没有活的英语前缀或后缀：它是从拉丁语 archivum 和希腊语 arkheion 整体借来的。英语随后在这个名词上构造出 archival、archivist、archivable 与 archivism，而复数 archives 是它的历史来源。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin archivum and its plural archiva meant written records and their repository. Greek arkheion 'town hall' and arkheia 'public records' are the deeper source, from arkhē 'government, beginning'.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语 archivum 及其复数 archiva 指书面记录及其存放处。更深的源头是希腊语 arkheion“市政厅”与 arkheia“公共记录”，出自 arkhē“政府、开端”。

items.meaning: records preserved as evidence, or the institution holding them
items.meaningCN: 作为证据保存的档案，或保管它们的机构（-es 为复数词尾）
items.example: The city's archives go back to the twelfth century.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市的档案可追溯到 12 世纪。

items.meaning: a collection of records, or to file into one
items.meaningCN: 档案集合；归档（由复数逆构出的单数）
items.exampleCN: 这批档案装满了三个房间。

items.meaning: relating to archives or suitable for long preservation
items.meaningCN: 档案的；适合长期保存的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: Store the negatives in archival sleeves.
items.exampleCN: 把底片存放在档案级保护套里。

items.meaning: a person who appraises and preserves archives
items.meaningCN: 档案管理员；档案学者（-ist 表示从业者）
items.example: The archivist refused to separate the two collections.
items.exampleCN: 档案管理员拒绝把这两批馆藏分开。

items.meaning: suitable or able to be archived
items.meaningCN: 可归档的；适合存档的（-able 表示能够）
items.example: Only the final drafts are archivable.

items.meaning: in archival terms or by archival methods
items.meaningCN: 在档案方面；以档案方式（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The papers were archivally boxed in acid-free card.
items.exampleCN: 这些文件用无酸纸盒按档案标准装好。

items.meaning: an orientation or practice centred on archiving
items.meaningCN: 档案主义；以存档为中心的做法（-ism 构成体系名词）
items.example: The artist's archivism turned every receipt into a work.
items.exampleCN: 这位艺术家的档案主义把每张收据都变成了作品。

items.meaning: the ongoing act or process of archiving
items.meaningCN: 归档工作；存档过程（-ing 构成过程名词）
items.example: Archiving the paper's website took three years.
items.exampleCN: 给这家报纸的网站存档花了三年。

items.meaning: filed away, or stored and no longer active
items.meaningCN: 已归档的；已存档、不再活跃的（-ed 构成分词或形容词）
items.example: The archived thread can still be searched.
items.exampleCN: 已存档的帖子仍然可以搜索。

items.meaning: the process of making something archival or of turning it into an archive
items.meaningCN: 档案化；使某物成为档案的过程（-ization 构成过程名词）
items.example: The archivization of everyday life is a modern habit.
items.exampleCN: 把日常生活档案化是一种现代习惯。

latinEntries.meaning: written records; the place where they are kept
latinEntries.meaningCN: 晚期拉丁语名词，复数 archiva：书面记录；存放处
晚期拉丁语复数：一批批书面记录
希腊语名词：市政厅、公共建筑
希腊语复数名词：公共记录

latinEntries.meaning: government, rule; literally beginning or first place
latinEntries.meaningCN: 希腊语名词：政府、统治；字面为开端或首位

definition_zh: n. 拱门通道；拱形门洞（可通行的拱下空间）
definition_en: A passage roofed by an arch, or the arched opening itself, so that people can walk through under the curve.
core_image: 头顶弯成一道拱，底下留出一条能走人的路
scene: 穿过那道拱门就是老城的集市。Beyond the archway lies the old town market.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：archway 指拱下可以通行的那条通道，重点在「能走过去」。

senses.title: A passage under an arch
senses.definition: a walkable space roofed by an arch, connecting one area to another
senses.definitionCN: 以拱为顶、可通行的空间，把一处与另一处连起来
senses.example: We stepped through the archway into a quiet courtyard.
senses.exampleCN: 我们穿过拱道，走进一个安静的院子。
senses.why: The word is arch plus way, so it names not the curve alone but the road that the curve makes possible.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 arch 加 way，所以它指的不只是那道弯，而是那道弯让出来的路。

senses.title: The arched opening as a structure
senses.definition: the arched entrance considered as a built feature, whether or not anyone passes through it
senses.definitionCN: 被当作建筑构件看待的拱形入口，不论是否有人从中通行
senses.example: The archway was carved with vines and birds.
senses.exampleCN: 拱门上雕着藤蔓与鸟。
senses.why: Here attention shifts from walking to building: the same opening is described as masonry rather than as a route.
senses.whyCN: 这里注意力从「走」转到「建」：同一个洞口被当作砌体而非路线来描述。

intro.en: Archway is arch plus way. Arch comes from Latin arcus, a bow, through Old French arche; way is native Old English weg. The compound is recorded in the eighteenth century.
intro.cn: archway 是 arch 加 way。arch 来自拉丁语 arcus「弓」，经古法语 arche；way 是古英语本族词 weg。这个复合词记录于 18 世纪。

items.en: Latin arcus meant a bow, and then any curved structure spanning a gap.
items.cn: 拉丁语 arcus 意为「弓」，进而指任何跨越缺口的弧形结构。

items.en: Old French arche named the curved span, the form that gave English arch.
items.cn: 古法语 arche 指弧形跨度，这个形式给出了英语 arch。

items.en: Middle English arche was used for bridges, doorways and the brows of a face alike.
items.cn: 中古英语 arche 同样用于桥、门洞与眉毛。

items.en: Way is native, from Old English weg, a road or course, cousin to German Weg.
items.cn: way 是本族词，来自古英语 weg「路、行程」，与德语 Weg 同源。

items.en: English joined the two in the eighteenth century to name a passage roofed by an arch.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪把两者合成，指以拱为顶的通道。

items.en: Today archway is the ordinary word for an arched entrance in gardens, campuses and old towns.
items.cn: 如今 archway 是园林、校园与老城中拱形入口的常用词。

note.en: The look-alike group separates arch, the curve alone, from archway, the passage under it; the near-meaning group lists other words for a way in.
note.cn: 形近组把只指弧形的 arch 与指拱下通道的 archway 分开；近义组列出其他表示入口的词。

entries.definition: A curved span over an opening.
entries.definitionCN: 洞口上方的弧形跨度。

entries.definition: A row of arches along a walk.
entries.definitionCN: 沿通道排列的一排拱。

entries.definition: Someone who shoots with a bow.
entries.definitionCN: 用弓射箭的人。

entries.definition: A main public road.
entries.definitionCN: 主要公路。

entries.definition: An opening that gives entry.
entries.definitionCN: 供进入的开口。

entries.definition: A grand doorway or entrance.
entries.definitionCN: 宏伟的门洞或入口。

entries.definition: A way through a building.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑内的通道。

entries.definition: An arched roof or ceiling.
entries.definitionCN: 拱形的顶或天花板。

normalIntro.en: Archway is arch plus way: the arch is the roof, the way is what you walk on underneath.
normalIntro.cn: archway 就是 arch 加 way：拱是顶，way 是你在底下走的那条路。

normal.en: Arch is the curve; archway is the passage under it.
normal.cn: arch 是那道弯，archway 是弯下的通道。

normal.en: An arcade is many arches in a row.
normal.cn: arcade 是一排连着的拱。

normal.en: Use through the archway, not across it.
normal.cn: 说 through the archway，不说 across it。

normal.en: It is countable: three stone archways.
normal.cn: 它可数：three stone archways。

normal.en: Vaulted archway stresses the arched roof.
normal.cn: vaulted archway 强调拱形的顶。

abstract.en: Picture a stone rainbow you can walk under.
abstract.cn: 想象一道能走过去的石头彩虹。

abstract.en: Imagine a courtyard framed by a curve.
abstract.cn: 想象被一道弯框住的院子。

abstract.en: Think of a doorway that is also a roof.
abstract.cn: 想象一个同时又是屋顶的门洞。

examples.en: Ivy had covered the whole archway.
examples.cn: 常春藤爬满了整个拱门。

examples.en: Two archways lead into the cloister.
examples.cn: 两道拱门通向回廊。

examples.en: The archways were rebuilt after the fire.
examples.cn: 火灾之后这些拱门被重建。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：arch「拱」+ way「路」——拱底下留出的那条路，就是拱门通道 archway。

root: 拉丁语 arcus「弓」经古法语 arche 成英语 arch「拱」，与古英语本族词 weg「路」在 18 世纪合成 archway，字面即「拱下的路」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one arched opening: the route you take through it, and the same opening seen as built masonry.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一个拱形洞口：你从中走过的路线，以及被当作砌体看待的同一个洞口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curve overhead with a walkable road left beneath it
core.cn: 核心意象：头顶弯成一道拱，底下留出一条能走人的路

branches.en: A step from street into courtyard.
Two archways leading to a cloister.
Vines and birds carved in stone.
Archways rebuilt after a fire.
Both are a curve with a gap below.
branches.cn: 两者都是底下留缺口的弯。

intro.en: Archway is a compound of arch and way; the bow root also builds arcade, archer and arched.
intro.cn: archway 是 arch 与 way 的复合词；「弓」词根还构成 arcade、archer 与 arched。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is arcus, a bow, and via, a road, which gives viaduct and deviate; way itself is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 arcus「弓」与 via「路」，后者产生 viaduct 与 deviate；way 本身是日耳曼词。

latinEntries.exampleCN: arcus 是 arch 的来源。

definition_zh: 热情的；炽热的；热烈的；忠心的
definition_en: showing very strong and eager feelings; passionate and enthusiastic
core_image: 胸中烧着一团不灭的火
scene: 雨夜里，游行队伍的火把仍未熄灭，年轻人喊得嗓子沙哑。He remained an ardent supporter of the reform.
sceneCN: 这里 ardent 是「热忱的、热烈的」（第 1 个义项：感情炽烈）；句意是他始终是这场改革的热情支持者。

derivatives.zh: ardent 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「热忱地」
ardent 加名词后缀 -y，义为「热情；炽热」
同源拉丁词 ardor 经法语进入英语，义为「热情；激情」
同出拉丁词根 ard-（燃烧），义为「艰巨的」，语义由「发热」引申为「费力」

senses.title: Showing intense eager emotion
senses.definition: feeling or expressing strong enthusiasm or devotion
senses.definitionCN: 怀有或表现出强烈的热忱、忠诚或激情
senses.example: She is an ardent advocate of animal rights.
senses.exampleCN: 她是动物权利的热心倡导者。
senses.why: The Latin root ardere means to burn, so feelings blaze like fire.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 ardere 意为「燃烧」，感情如火焰般炽烈。

senses.title: Burning with passionate love
senses.definition: full of passionate desire, especially in romantic contexts
senses.definitionCN: 充满炽烈欲望的，多用于爱情语境
senses.example: He wrote her an ardent love letter at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 午夜时分他给她写了一封火热的情书。
senses.why: Romantic passion is the hottest human fire, keeping the burning image intact.
senses.whyCN: 爱情激情是人类最炽热的火，完整保留「燃烧」意象。

senses.title: Glowing or burning hot, of things
senses.definition: giving out great heat; literally burning, in older or literary usage
senses.definitionCN: 发出高热的；字面燃烧之义，今存于旧式或文学用法
senses.example: The desert sent up ardent waves of heat at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 正午的沙漠腾起灼人的热浪。
senses.why: This is the original physical sense from which the emotional sense grew.
senses.whyCN: 这是本义，情感义正由物理的「灼热」引申而来。

intro.en: Ardent comes straight from Latin ardens, the present participle of ardere, to burn.
intro.cn: ardent 直接源自拉丁语 ardens，即动词 ardere（燃烧）的现在分词。

items.en: The root *as- / *as-dh- is reconstructed as meaning to burn, glow.
items.cn: 重构词根 *as-/*as-dh- 义为「燃烧、发光」（重构形式）。

items.en: Ardere meant to burn; ardens meant burning, glowing, then eager, passionate.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ardere 意为「燃烧」；ardens 由「燃烧的」引申为「热切的、多情的」。

items.en: Old French ardant carried both the fire sense and the passion sense.
items.cn: 古法语 ardant 同时保有「火的」与「热忱的」两义。

items.en: Ardent entered Middle English in Chaucer's time with both senses.
items.cn: 乔叟时代，ardent 带着两义进入中古英语。

items.en: Today the emotional sense dominates; the literal burning sense is rare and literary.
items.cn: 现代英语以情感义为主，字面「灼热」义已罕用且偏文学。

note.en: Ardent belongs to a Latin fire family; keep it apart from look-alike arduous.
note.cn: ardent 属拉丁「火」词族，须与形近词 arduous 区分。

entries.definition: requiring great effort; difficult
entries.definitionCN: 费力的、艰巨的，同出 ardere 词根但语义转向「费力」

entries.definition: a forest region in Shakespeare's plays, and a place name
entries.definitionCN: 莎士比亚剧中的阿登森林及地名，只是拼写相近，并非同词

entries.definition: great warmth of feeling; enthusiasm
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的热忱，ardent 的同根名词

entries.definition: showing intense feeling or desire
entries.definitionCN: 情感强烈的，与 ardent 的核心义几乎重合

entries.definition: having or showing very strong sincere feeling
entries.definitionCN: 炽热而诚挚的，同属「火喻感情」词族

entries.definition: showing great energy and enthusiasm for a cause
entries.definitionCN: 为事业满腔热忱的，侧重行动上的狂热

normalIntro.en: Link ardent to the Latin fire family through ar-, ard-.
normalIntro.cn: 通过 ar-、ard- 词根把 ardent 联到拉丁「火」词族。

normal.en: ardere = to burn; an ardent heart is a burning heart.
normal.cn: ardere 意为「燃烧」，ardent 的心即燃烧的心。

normal.en: Ardor is the noun: political ardor.
normal.cn: 名词是 ardor：政治热情。

normal.en: Arduous shares the root but means hard work, not hot feelings.
normal.cn: arduous 同根但指费力的工作，不是热烈的感情。

normal.en: An ardent fan never stops cheering.
normal.cn: 狂热的粉丝从不停下喝彩。

normal.en: Ardently is the adverb: ardently hoped.
normal.cn: 副词是 ardently：热切地希望。

abstract.en: Picture a torch that will not go out in the rain, like undying loyalty.
abstract.cn: 想象雨中不灭的火炬，如同不熄的忠诚。

abstract.en: Feel your chest glowing warm when you argue for what you love.
abstract.cn: 感受为所爱之事辩护时胸口发热的温度。

abstract.en: See sparks flying from two debaters' eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象辩论者眼中迸出的火花。

examples.en: The ardent young reformer toured the country giving speeches.
examples.cn: 这位热忱的年轻改革者巡回全国发表演讲。

examples.en: Their ardent friendship survived twenty years apart.
examples.cn: 他们炽热的友谊历经二十年分离而未减。

examples.en: An ardent glow rose from the forge.
examples.cn: 锻炉里腾起炽热的光。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿凳」——他热情似火，坐哪儿都嫌冷板凳，一屁股把铁凳都坐热了，真是「阿凳」般的热心肠。

root: 拉丁语 ardere（燃烧）→ 现在分词 ardens（燃烧的 → 热切的）；同族词有 arduous、ardor、arson。

sensesIntro.en: From literal burning heat to blazing emotion and blazing love.
sensesIntro.cn: 由字面的灼热延伸到炽烈的情感与炽热的爱情。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heart on fire that never cools
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗永不冷却的燃烧之心

branches.en: emotion blazing like flame
romantic fire between lovers
the literal heat that seeded the metaphor
devotion burning without pause
heat as the shared root image

intro.en: The Latin root ard- (burn) links fire words and passion words.
intro.cn: 拉丁词根 ard-（燃烧）串联起「火」与「激情」两类词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ardere and its compounds passed into French and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ardere 及其复合词经法语进入英语。

definition_zh: n. 热情，激情，热切（英式拼作 ardour）；（旧用）灼热，炽热
definition_en: Intense enthusiasm or passion for a person, cause or activity; in older use, burning heat. British English spells it ardour.
core_image: 胸口那团一直烧着的火
scene: 他把全部热情投进了这项研究。He threw all his ardor into the research.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：ardor 指对人、事业或活动强烈的热情，英式拼写为 ardour。

senses.title: Burning enthusiasm
senses.definition: strong, eager feeling for a person, belief or work, the sense almost always intended today
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、某信念或某项工作强烈而急切的感情，是今天几乎唯一使用的义项
senses.example: She defended the plan with unexpected ardor.
senses.exampleCN: 她以出人意料的热情为该计划辩护。
senses.why: The Latin root means burn, so ardor is feeling described as fire: it warms, it spreads and it can go out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「烧」，所以 ardor 是把感情当火来写：它会发热、会蔓延，也会熄灭。

senses.title: Physical burning heat
senses.definition: in older or poetic use, intense heat itself, the literal sense the figurative one grew from
senses.definitionCN: 在较旧或诗歌用法中指强烈的热本身，是比喻义所由来的字面义
senses.example: The poem speaks of the ardor of the noon sun.
senses.exampleCN: 诗中写到正午太阳的灼热。
senses.why: This is the older layer: before ardor meant eagerness it meant temperature, which is why ardent still describes both.
senses.whyCN: 这是较古的一层：ardor 在指热切之前先指温度，所以 ardent 至今两者都能形容。

intro.en: Ardor is Latin ardor, flame or eagerness, from ardere, to burn. English took it through Old French ardour, and American spelling later dropped the u.
intro.cn: ardor 就是拉丁语 ardor「火焰、热切」，来自 ardere「燃烧」。英语经古法语 ardour 吸收，美式拼写后来去掉了 u。

items.en: The reconstructed root as- meant to burn or glow, and it also lies behind ash and arid.
items.cn: 重构词根 as- 意为「燃烧、发光」，它也是 ash 与 arid 的来源。

items.en: Latin ardere meant to be on fire, and its participle ardens gave English ardent.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ardere 意为「着火」，其分词 ardens 给出英语 ardent。

items.en: The noun ardor named a flame, then heat, then the heat of feeling, all in one word.
items.cn: 名词 ardor 先指火焰，再指热，再指感情的热度，都在同一个词里。

items.en: Old French ardour carried the word north with the u that British spelling still keeps.
items.cn: 古法语 ardour 带着那个 u 北上，英式拼写至今保留。

items.en: English recorded the word in the fourteenth century for both burning heat and eager passion.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪记录该词，兼指灼热与热切的激情。

items.en: American reform dropped the u to give ardor, while British usage kept ardour; both are correct.
items.cn: 美式改革去掉 u 成 ardor，英式保留 ardour，两者都对。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against order and odor, which only look similar, and arduous, which has a different root; the near-meaning group lists words for strong feeling.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与只是形似的 order、odor 以及词根不同的 arduous 混淆；近义组列出表示强烈感情的词。

entries.definition: Burning with enthusiasm.
entries.definitionCN: 热情如火的。

entries.definition: Arrangement, or a command.
entries.definitionCN: 次序；命令。

entries.definition: A smell, especially a bad one.
entries.definitionCN: 气味，尤指臭味。

entries.definition: Demanding great effort.
entries.definitionCN: 需要极大努力的。

entries.definition: Very strong feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 极强烈的感情。

entries.definition: Eager devotion to a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 对事业的热忱投入。

entries.definition: Intense warmth of feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 感情的炽热。

entries.definition: Lively interest and eagerness.
entries.definitionCN: 活跃的兴趣与热切。

normalIntro.en: Ardor is ard-, burn, plus -or, a state: the state of burning inside, which is what enthusiasm feels like.
normalIntro.cn: ardor 就是 ard-「烧」加 -or「状态」：心里烧着的状态，正是热情的感觉。

normal.en: American ardor, British ardour; pick one and stay consistent.
normal.cn: 美式 ardor，英式 ardour；选一种并保持一致。

normal.en: It is uncountable: say great ardor, not an ardor.
normal.cn: 它不可数：说 great ardor，不说 an ardor。

normal.en: The adjective is ardent, the adverb ardently.
normal.cn: 形容词是 ardent，副词是 ardently。

normal.en: Use ardor for plus the cause or person.
normal.cn: 用 ardor for 加事业或人。

normal.en: Arid shares the burning root but means dry.
normal.cn: arid 共享「烧」词根，但意为干旱。

abstract.en: Picture a coal that stays red overnight.
abstract.cn: 想象一块整夜通红的炭。

abstract.en: Imagine a speech that warms a cold hall.
abstract.cn: 想象一场把冷厅讲热的演说。

abstract.en: Think of a fire that dies when nobody feeds it.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆没人添柴就熄的火。

examples.en: His ardor for reform never cooled.
examples.cn: 他对改革的热情从未冷却。

examples.en: The volunteers worked with real ardor.
examples.cn: 志愿者们带着真正的热情工作。

examples.en: Early ardor gave way to steady routine.
examples.cn: 起初的热情让位于平稳的日常。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：ard-「烧」+ -or「状态」——心里一直烧着的状态，就是热情 ardor。

root: 原始印欧词根 as-「烧」生出拉丁 ardere「燃烧」，名词 ardor「火焰、热切」经古法语 ardour 进入英语；美式去掉 u 拼作 ardor，同族还有 ardent 与 arid。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one fire: heat you can measure, and the same heat used as a name for eager feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一团火：能测量的热，以及被借来称呼热切感情的同一种热。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the fire in the chest that keeps on burning
core.cn: 核心意象：胸口那团一直烧着的火

branches.en: A speech that warms a cold hall.
Volunteers who never slow down.
The noon sun beating on stone.
branches.cn: 正午晒在石头上的太阳。

branches.en: A coal still red at dawn.
Both are heat, literal or felt.
branches.cn: 两者都是热，实际的或感到的。

intro.en: Ardor is the burn root ard- plus -or; the same root builds ardent, ardently and, through drying, arid and aridity.
intro.cn: ardor 是「烧」词根 ard- 加 -or；同一词根构成 ardent、ardently，并经「干」义构成 arid 与 aridity。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is ardere, to burn, ardor, flame, and aridus, dry, which gives arid and aridity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 ardere「燃烧」、ardor「火焰」与 aridus「干的」，后者产生 arid 与 aridity。

latinEntries.meaning: to burn, to be on fire

definition_zh: 艰巨的；费力的；辛勤的；险峻的
definition_en: requiring great effort and energy; difficult and tiring
core_image: 陡坡上背着石头一步步往上爬
scene: 山道上雾气弥漫，登山者每人背着几十斤的装备。They began the arduous climb to the summit.
sceneCN: 这里 arduous 是「艰巨费力的」（第 1 个义项：需要极大努力）；句意是他们开始向峰顶艰难攀登。

derivatives.zh: arduous 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「费力地」
arduous 加名词后缀 -ness，义为「艰巨性」
同出拉丁词根 ard-，义为「热忱的」，与费力义同源异向

senses.title: Requiring great effort
senses.definition: demanding sustained physical or mental exertion
senses.definitionCN: 需要持续的身体或精神上的巨大努力
senses.example: Rebuilding the library after the fire was an arduous task.
senses.exampleCN: 火灾后重建图书馆是一项艰巨的任务。
senses.why: Steep ground makes burning effort; the heat root points to strained labor.
senses.whyCN: 陡坡令人「燃烧」般费力，词根本义指向耗竭体力的劳作。

senses.title: Hard to traverse, of routes
senses.definition: steep, rough and exhausting to travel along, said of paths and journeys
senses.definitionCN: 形容道路陡峭崎岖、行走起来令人筋疲力尽
senses.example: The mule track is the only arduous route into the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 这条骡道是进谷唯一艰险的路线。
senses.why: The difficulty of terrain is the concrete source of the effort sense.
senses.whyCN: 地形的艰难是「费力」义的具体来源。

senses.title: Painstaking and long-drawn-out
senses.titleCN: 长期辛劳的；旷日持久的
senses.definition: lasting long and demanding patient, repeated effort
senses.definitionCN: 历时长久且需要耐心反复付出的
senses.example: Decades of arduous research finally produced the vaccine.
senses.exampleCN: 数十年的艰辛研究终于研制出疫苗。
senses.why: Effort stretched over time still keeps the image of strained exertion.
senses.whyCN: 把力气拉长到岁月里，仍是「耗竭式付出」意象的延伸。

intro.en: Arduous descends from Latin arduus, steep or high, later felt as laborious.
intro.cn: arduous 源自拉丁语 arduus，本义「陡峭、高耸」，后引申为「费力的」。

items.en: The root *gher- or a related form is reconstructed as tall, steep.
items.cn: 词根 *gher- 或相关形式被重构为「高的、陡的」（重构形式）。

items.en: Arduus meant steep, high; arduus labor in Virgil means a steep, uphill task.
items.cn: 拉丁语 arduus 意为「陡峭的」；维吉尔笔下 arduus labor 即「陡坡般的劳作」。

items.en: Roman writers extended arduus from steep paths to difficult undertakings.
items.cn: 罗马作家把 arduus 从陡峭道路扩展到艰难事业。

items.en: The word entered English via French ardueux with the effort sense dominant.
items.cn: 该词经法语 ardueux 进入英语，费力义已成主导。

items.en: Arduous now chiefly describes demanding tasks, journeys and negotiations.
items.cn: 现代英语中 arduous 主要形容艰巨的任务、旅程与谈判。

note.en: Do not confuse arduous with ardent: one tires the body, the other fires the heart.
note.cn: 别把 arduous 与 ardent 混淆：一个累坏身体，一个点燃心火。

entries.definition: very enthusiastic and passionate

entries.definition: slow to understand; blunt
entries.definitionCN: 迟钝的，只是词尾拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: intense enthusiasm or passion
entries.definitionCN: 炽热的情感，与 arduous 同根但属情感域

entries.definition: requiring much time and hard work
entries.definitionCN: 耗时耗力的，与 arduous 的核心义高度重合

entries.definition: needing great energy and effort

entries.definitionCN: 把人榨干的、极其累人的，程度比 arduous 更强

normalIntro.en: Split the word as ardu- (steep) + -ous to recall the meaning.
normalIntro.cn: 把词拆成 ardu-（陡）加 -ous 来记义。

normal.en: Latin arduus = steep; a steep road is an arduous road.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 arduus 意为「陡」：陡路即艰辛之路。

normal.en: Keep arduous (hard) apart from ardent (hot-hearted).
normal.cn: 区分 arduous（艰难）与 ardent（热忱）。

normal.en: An arduous task drains you like climbing a cliff.
normal.cn: 艰巨任务如攀崖般耗尽气力。

normal.en: Negotiations are often described as arduous.
normal.cn: 谈判常被形容为 arduous（艰难漫长）。

normal.en: Arduously is the adverb: work arduously.
normal.cn: 副词是 arduously：勤勉辛苦地工作。

abstract.en: Picture a mountain so steep each step burns your legs.
abstract.cn: 想象陡得每一步都烧腿的高山。

abstract.en: Feel sweat dripping on a ledger you must finish before dawn.
abstract.cn: 感受黎明前赶账本时滴落的汗珠。

abstract.en: See a long uphill road vanishing into clouds.
abstract.cn: 想象一条没入云端的漫长上坡路。

examples.en: The engineers finished their arduous survey of the canyon.
examples.cn: 工程师们完成了对峡谷的艰苦勘测。

examples.en: Learning the language took years of arduous practice.
examples.cn: 掌握这门语言花了多年刻苦练习。

examples.en: They chose the arduous northern route through the mountains.
examples.cn: 他们选择了穿越群山的艰险北线。

definition_zh: 争论；争辩；论证；主张
definition_en: to disagree in words, to give reasons for an opinion, or to persuade someone by reasoning
core_image: 两个人隔着桌子各说各的理由
scene: 饭桌上两个人声音越来越高。They argued about who should pay the bill.
sceneCN: 这里 argue 是「争论」（第 1 个义项：因意见不合而口头冲突）；句意是他们为谁该付账争了起来。

senses.title: To disagree in words
senses.definition: to speak angrily with someone who disagrees
senses.definitionCN: 与意见不同的人激烈地说话
senses.example: They argued about who should pay the bill.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为谁该付账争了起来。
senses.why: Latin arguere meant 'to make clear by reasoning'; when two people each press their case, clarity turns into conflict.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 arguere 意为「通过论证说清楚」；当双方各自坚持说法时，说清就变成了冲突。

senses.title: To give reasons for a view
senses.definition: to present evidence and reasoning in support of an opinion
senses.definitionCN: 提出证据与推理来支持某个观点
senses.example: The report argues that the plan will save money.
senses.exampleCN: 报告论证说这项计划能省钱。
senses.why: This keeps the original Latin sense: to argue is to lay out proofs so that a conclusion becomes clear.
senses.whyCN: 这一义保留了拉丁语原义：argue 就是摆出证据，使结论变得清楚。

senses.title: To persuade by reasoning
senses.definition: to bring someone to a decision through argument
senses.definitionCN: 通过论理使人作出某个决定
senses.example: She argued him into taking the job.
senses.exampleCN: 她说服他接受了这份工作。
senses.why: If reasons can make a point clear, they can also move a listener to act, which gives the persuasive sense.
senses.whyCN: 既然理由能让观点变清楚，也就能推动听者行动，于是产生「说服」义。

core_image: 两张纸上的理由被并排摆着对照
scene: 两人从厨房吵到客厅。Their argument lasted until midnight.

senses.title: An angry disagreement
senses.definition: a heated exchange between people who disagree
senses.definitionCN: 意见不合的人之间激烈的言语往来
senses.example: Their argument lasted until midnight.

definition_zh: 干旱的；干燥的；荒芜的；（文风、话题）枯燥无味的；缺乏感情的
definition_en: having so little rain that few plants can grow; also dry and uninteresting in style or feeling
core_image: 裂成多边形的黏土上，一丛带刺灌木孤零零地立着，天空白得没有云
scene: 裂开的黏土与带刺灌丛覆盖着这片干旱的平原。Cracked clay and thorny scrub covered the arid plain.
sceneCN: 这里 arid 指「降雨极少、植物难以生长的」（第 1 个义项：干旱气候或地区）；句意为裂开的黏土与带刺灌丛覆盖着这片干旱的平原。图中可辨识物件：多边形干裂缝、带刺灌丛、白色天空、砾石。

pos.zh: 干旱的；干燥的；荒芜的；枯燥的；无感情的

senses.title: A climate of very low rainfall
senses.definition: describing a climate whose annual rainfall is too low to support rain-fed agriculture or continuous vegetation
senses.definitionCN: 形容年降水太低、无法支持雨养农业或连续植被的气候
senses.example: Cracked clay and thorny scrub covered the arid plain.
senses.exampleCN: 裂开的黏土与带刺灌丛覆盖着这片干旱的平原。
senses.why: arid enters English from Latin aridus 'dry, parched', whose root image is a surface dried out by sun.
senses.whyCN: arid 来自拉丁 aridus「干燥、烤干」，其词根意象是被太阳晒干的地表。

senses.title: Dry and barren ground
senses.definition: describing land that holds little moisture and bears few plants, whether or not it is officially a desert
senses.definitionCN: 形容蓄水少、植物稀少的地，无论是否正式算作荒漠
senses.example: Nothing will grow on that arid slope without irrigation.
senses.exampleCN: 那片干旱坡地不灌溉什么也长不出来。
senses.why: the adjective describes a condition of the ground, while desert is a place and desertification is a process.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词描述地面的状态，而 desert 是地方、desertification 是过程。

senses.title: Arid soil chemistry
senses.definition: soil low in organic matter, often alkaline, with salt or calcium carbonate layers near the surface
senses.definitionCN: 有机质低、常偏碱，表层附近有盐层或碳酸钙层的土壤
senses.example: Arid soil forms a hard caliche layer that roots cannot pass.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱土壤形成坚硬的钙积层，根穿不过去。
senses.why: little rain means little leaching, so salts and carbonates stay where they form.
senses.whyCN: 雨少意味着淋洗少，盐与碳酸盐就留在原处。

senses.title: Hyper-arid extremes
senses.definition: the most severe dryness class, where rain may not fall for years and life survives only in rare niches
senses.definitionCN: 最严重的干旱等级，可能多年无雨，生命只在极少数微生境中存活
senses.example: Parts of the Atacama are hyper-arid rather than merely arid.
senses.exampleCN: 阿塔卡马的部分地区属于超干旱，而不只是干旱。
senses.why: classification needs degrees, so arid gained a marked upper extreme with its own prefix.
senses.whyCN: 分类需要等级，于是 arid 加前缀形成标记出的上端。

senses.title: The semi-arid transition
senses.definition: the zone between arid and subhumid where rainfall supports grass but not closed forest
senses.definitionCN: 介于干旱与半湿润之间、降水足以长草却不足以成林的带
senses.example: Semi-arid country can flip from crop to dust within one season.
senses.exampleCN: 半干旱地区能在一个季节内从庄稼变成尘土。
senses.why: the prefix semi- marks the boundary where the adjective stops applying strictly, and that boundary is the fragile zone.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 semi- 标出该形容词不再严格适用的界线，而这条界线正是脆弱地带。

senses.title: Dry and dull in style
senses.definition: describing writing, speech or a subject that is dry, lifeless and without interest
senses.definitionCN: 形容文字、言谈或话题干瘪、无生气、引不起兴趣
senses.example: The report was accurate but arid, page after page of figures.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告准确却枯燥，一页接一页的数字。
senses.why: the metaphor borrows the physical sense: a text with no rain has no growth in it.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻借物理义：没有雨的文字里也长不出东西。

senses.title: Emotionally dry
senses.definition: describing a manner or relationship that shows no warmth, feeling or imaginative sympathy
senses.definitionCN: 形容态度或关系没有温度、感情或想象性的体谅
senses.example: An arid handshake ended the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 一次毫无温度的握手结束了会面。
senses.why: the same dryness moves from land to people: nothing nourishing passes between them.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「干」从土地移到人身上：彼此之间没有任何滋养性的东西传递。

senses.title: Arid-zone ecology
senses.definition: the study and description of dryland communities, whose plants evade, resist or store scarce water
senses.definitionCN: 对旱地群落的研究与描述，其植物回避、抵抗或储存稀缺的水
senses.example: Arid-zone plants often carry waxy leaves and deep taproots.
senses.exampleCN: 旱区植物常具蜡质叶与深主根。
senses.why: as a compound modifier, arid labels a whole branch of ecology defined by water scarcity.
senses.whyCN: 作复合修饰语时，arid 标出以缺水为定义的一整个生态学分支。

intro.en: Arid comes straight from Latin aridus 'dry, parched', built on the verb arere 'to be dry', so its Latin line is short and well documented.
intro.cn: arid 直接来自拉丁 aridus「干燥、烤干」，由动词 arere「干燥」构成，其拉丁线索短且有文献。

items.en: Arere meant 'to be dry or parched'. It also underlies arefacere 'to dry up', seen in English arefaction.
items.cn: arere 意为「干燥、被烤干」。它也构成 arefacere「使干」，英语 arefaction 即由此来。

items.en: The adjective aridus described ground, air or a person dried out; it is the direct source of English arid.
items.cn: 形容词 aridus 描述被晒干的地、空气或人；它是英语 arid 的直接来源。

items.en: English took arid in the sixteenth century, at first in the physical sense of parched ground, with the figurative sense following later.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入 arid，最初指物理上被烤干的地，比喻义随后出现。

items.en: Modern climatology fixed arid as a measurable zone, usually below about 250 mm of rain a year, and added semi- and hyper- grades.
items.cn: 现代气候学把 arid 固定为可测的带，通常年降水低于约 250 毫米，并加上 semi- 与 hyper- 等级。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin root): the Indo-European root commonly reconstructed as *as- 'to burn, glow' is a reconstruction, and the exact first English citation is not securely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（拉丁语之前词根）：通常重构的印欧词根 *as-「燃烧、发光」属重构形式；最早英语书证年代亦不可靠。

note.en: Group one separates the arid family and its near spellings; group two separates the physical and figurative synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组区分 arid 词族与相近拼写；第二组区分物理义与比喻义的同义词。

entries.definition: The noun for the state of being arid, both climatic and stylistic.
entries.definitionCN: 表示干旱状态的名词，兼指气候与文风。

entries.definition: The adverb, usually in the figurative sense of speaking or writing without warmth.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，通常用于说话或写作缺乏温度的比喻义。

entries.definition: A rarer synonym of aridity; it is correct but much less frequent.
entries.definitionCN: aridity 的较罕用同义词；正确但频率低得多。

entries.definition: Half-dry: the transition zone that is dry but not yet desert.
entries.definitionCN: 半干燥：干旱但尚未成荒漠的过渡带。

entries.definition: The plain word for lacking moisture; arid is its technical and often more severe counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 表示缺水的日常词；arid 是它技术化、通常更严重的对应词。

entries.definition: Dried out to cracking, used of soil, lips or throat; it stresses visible damage.
entries.definitionCN: 干到开裂，用于土壤、嘴唇或喉咙；强调可见的损伤。

entries.definition: Unable to bear crops or young; it is about productivity, not rainfall.
entries.definitionCN: 不能产作物或后代；讲的是生产力，不是降水。

entries.definition: A place, not a quality; a desert is arid, but arid land need not be a desert.
entries.definitionCN: 是地方而非性质；荒漠必干旱，但干旱地不必是荒漠。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin arere 'be dry' → aridus → arid: the shortest possible line.
normal.cn: 拉丁 arere「干燥」→ aridus → arid：最短的一条线。

normal.en: The family runs arid, aridity, aridly, aridness, semi-arid.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 arid、aridity、aridly、aridness、semi-arid。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: arid climate, arid region, arid soil, semi-arid.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：干旱气候、干旱地区、干旱土壤、半干旱。

normal.en: The metaphor is the same dryness applied to prose and manners.
normal.cn: 比喻就是把同一种「干」用在文章与举止上。

normal.en: The image is cracked clay under a white sky with one thorn bush.
normal.cn: 意象是白空之下一片裂开的黏土，只有一丛刺灌。

abstract.en: Think of a sponge left in the sun until it is hard.
abstract.cn: 想象一块海绵被晒到发硬。

abstract.en: Think of a conversation where nothing green ever comes up.
abstract.cn: 想象一场谈话里始终长不出一点绿色。

abstract.en: Think of a page so dry that the words crack apart.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸干到字都裂开。

examples.en: Arid regions cover roughly a third of the land surface.
examples.cn: 干旱地区约占陆地表面的三分之一。

examples.en: The lecture was learned but arid.
examples.cn: 那场讲座很有学问，却枯燥无味。

examples.en: Arid air sucked the moisture from the washing.
examples.cn: 干燥的空气把洗过的衣物水分吸干了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「a-rid」联想「啊，rid（去掉）了水」——水被晒没了 → 干旱的

root: 拉丁 arere「干燥、被烤干」→ 形容词 aridus「干燥的」→ 英语 arid。通常重构的印欧词根 *as-「燃烧、发光」属重构形式，并非定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses carry one dryness from climate and soil into extreme grades, then into style, feeling and the ecology that studies it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一种「干」从气候与土壤，带到极端等级，再带到文风、感情与研究它的生态学。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a surface baked hard by sun with too little water to support growth.
core.cn: 核心意象：被太阳烤硬的地表，水少到长不出东西。

branches.en: CLIMATE GRADES: arid is a zone, and semi-arid marks where it fades.
branches.cn: 气候等级：arid 是一个带，semi-arid 标出它消退之处。

branches.en: SEVERITY: from barren ground to years without rain, the same quality deepens.
branches.cn: 强度：从贫瘠地面到多年无雨，同一种性质不断加深。

branches.en: SOIL AND FLORA: little leaching leaves salt, and plants evolve wax and deep roots.
branches.cn: 土壤与植物：淋洗少留下盐，植物演化出蜡质与深根。

branches.en: STYLE: a text without rain has no growth, so it is called arid.
branches.cn: 文风：没有雨的文字长不出东西，因此被称作「干」。

branches.en: FEELING: the same dryness reaches manners and relationships.
branches.cn: 感情：同一种「干」延伸到举止与关系。

intro.en: Arid is a Latin adjective stem that takes English noun and adverb suffixes, and a semi- prefix for the transition zone.
intro.cn: arid 是拉丁形容词词干，可接英语名词与副词后缀，并可用 semi- 前缀表示过渡带。

latinIntro.en: Latin arere 'be dry' and aridus 'dry' are both documented; the deeper Indo-European root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 arere「干燥」与 aridus「干燥的」均有文献；更深的印欧词根属重构。

items.example: Aridity is measured by rainfall against evaporation.
items.exampleCN: 干旱度以降水和蒸发相比来衡量。
他干巴巴地回答，毫无温度。

items.example: The aridness of the air preserved the wood.
items.exampleCN: 空气干燥使木头得以保存。

items.example: Semi-arid grassland feeds cattle in good years.
items.exampleCN: 半干旱草原在好年景能养牛。

items.example: Hyper-arid deserts may go years without rain.
items.exampleCN: 超干旱荒漠可能多年无雨。

items.example: Arid-zone soils are thin in humus.
Arefaction follows once the marsh is drained.
items.exampleCN: 湿地排干后便出现干燥过程。

definition_zh: 干旱；干旱度；干燥；（文风、情感）枯燥、冷淡
definition_en: the condition of being extremely dry, measured as the balance between rainfall and water loss; also dryness of style or feeling
core_image: 一排雨量筒和一只蒸发皿立在空地上，两组读数相差很大，干旱程度就被写成一个数
scene: 雨量筒与蒸发皿给出同一个数字，用来表示这个流域的干旱程度。Rain gauges and evaporation pans give a single number for the aridity of the basin.
sceneCN: 这里 aridity 指「降水与蒸发之间的亏缺程度」（第 1 个义项：气候干旱度）；句意为雨量筒与蒸发皿共同给出一个数字，表示该流域的干旱程度。图中可辨识物件：雨量筒、蒸发皿、记录板、干裂地面。

pos.zh: 干旱；干旱度；干燥（不可数）

senses.title: Climatic dryness as a deficit
senses.definition: the condition of a climate in which potential water loss by evaporation exceeds precipitation over the year
senses.definitionCN: 全年蒸发造成的水分损失超过降水的气候状态
senses.example: Rain gauges and evaporation pans give a single number for the aridity of the basin.
senses.exampleCN: 雨量筒与蒸发皿共同给出一个数字，表示该流域的干旱程度。
senses.why: aridity is a relationship, not a quantity of rain alone: the same rainfall is wet in a cool place and dry in a hot one.
senses.whyCN: 干旱是一种关系，而不只是雨量：同样的雨在凉处算湿，在热处算干。

senses.title: The aridity index
senses.definition: a numerical ratio, commonly precipitation divided by potential evapotranspiration, used to classify dry climates
senses.definitionCN: 常用降水除以潜在蒸散量的比值，用于划分干旱气候
senses.example: An aridity index below 0.05 marks the hyper-arid zone.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱指数低于 0.05 标为超干旱带。
senses.why: once aridity is defined as a ratio, it becomes a number that maps and policy can use.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把干旱定义为比值，它就变成地图与政策可用的数字。

senses.title: Moisture deficit in soil and air
senses.titleCN: 土壤与空气的水分亏缺
senses.definition: the dryness of soil or air measured as the shortfall between what could be held and what is present
senses.definitionCN: 土壤或空气的干燥，以可持水量与实际含水量的差额衡量
senses.example: Soil aridity deepened as the organic matter wore away.
senses.exampleCN: 随着有机质流失，土壤干旱程度加深。
senses.why: the same noun covers the medium as well as the climate, because both are defined by a shortfall.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也覆盖介质本身，因为两者都由亏缺定义。

senses.title: A gradient of ecological harshness
senses.titleCN: 生态严酷度的干旱梯度
senses.definition: the ordering of sites from moist to extremely dry along which species composition and cover change
senses.definitionCN: 从湿润到极干的地点排序，物种组成与覆盖沿此改变
senses.example: Species richness falls steadily along the aridity gradient.
senses.exampleCN: 物种丰富度沿干旱梯度稳定下降。
senses.why: ecologists treat aridity as a continuous axis, so one noun describes a whole sequence of habitats.
senses.whyCN: 生态学者把干旱当作连续轴，因此一个名词描述一整串生境。

senses.title: Hydrological dryness of a catchment
senses.definition: the tendency of a catchment to yield little runoff because most rain is evaporated or stored
senses.definitionCN: 流域因大部分降水被蒸发或蓄住而产流很少的倾向
senses.example: High aridity keeps the river dry for most of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 高干旱度使这条河一年中大部分时间断流。
senses.why: water managers use aridity for the balance of a whole basin, not only for the air above it.
senses.whyCN: 水利管理者用干旱度描述整个流域的收支，而不只是其上方的空气。

senses.title: Dryness of style
senses.definition: a quality of writing or speech that is dull, unadorned and without imaginative life
senses.definitionCN: 文字或言谈乏味、无修饰、缺乏想象生气的性质
senses.example: The aridity of the prose made the evidence hard to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 行文枯燥，使证据难以跟上。
senses.why: the metaphor treats a text as ground: no rain, no growth, no colour.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻把文本当作土地：没有雨，就没有生长与颜色。

senses.title: Emotional coldness
senses.definition: an absence of warmth, sympathy or feeling in a manner or relationship
senses.definitionCN: 态度或关系中缺少温度、同情或感情
senses.example: There was an aridity in his voice that discouraged questions.
senses.exampleCN: 他声音里有一种冷淡，让人不敢提问。
senses.why: dryness transfers from climate to temperament because both describe a place where nothing nourishing grows.
senses.whyCN: 「干」从气候转到性情，因为两者都描述长不出滋养之物的地方。

senses.title: A field barren of new ideas
senses.definition: the state of a subject or discipline that has stopped producing fresh work or interest
senses.definitionCN: 某学科或话题停止产生新成果或新趣味的状况
senses.example: Critics complained of the aridity of the debate.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者抱怨这场辩论贫乏无物。
senses.why: the abstract sense extends the metaphor once more: a field can be dry just as land can.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把比喻再推一层：领域也能像土地一样「干」。

intro.en: Aridity is the Latin abstract noun ariditas, from aridus 'dry' plus -itas '-ity'; English took it nearly unchanged in form.
intro.cn: aridity 就是拉丁抽象名词 ariditas，由 aridus「干燥」加 -itas「-ity」构成；英语几乎原样借入。

items.en: Arere 'to be dry' supplies the root; its participle aridus described parched ground or air.
items.cn: arere「干燥」提供词根；其分词 aridus 描述被烤干的地或空气。

items.en: Ariditas 'dryness' added -itas, the suffix that turns an adjective into a state noun, to aridus.
items.cn: ariditas「干燥」在 aridus 上加 -itas，即把形容词变成状态名词的后缀。

items.en: English uses aridity from the seventeenth century, at first for physical dryness and later for style.
items.cn: 英语自 17 世纪使用 aridity，最初指物理干燥，后来也指文风。

items.en: Twentieth-century climatology defined aridity quantitatively through precipitation and potential evapotranspiration.
items.cn: 20 世纪气候学用降水与潜在蒸散量对干旱度做定量定义。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin root and first date): the Indo-European root behind arere is reconstructed, not attested, and the earliest English citation is not securely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（拉丁语之前词根与首见年代）：arere 背后的印欧词根属重构而非有文献；最早英语书证年代不可靠。

note.en: Group one separates the arid family; group two separates dryness words that are not climatic states.
note.cn: 第一组区分 arid 词族；第二组区分并非气候状态的「干」词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning dry or dull; aridity is the noun built from it.
entries.definitionCN: 意为干旱或枯燥的形容词；aridity 是由它构成的名词。

entries.definition: The adverb, most often used of speaking or writing without warmth.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，最常用于说话或写作缺乏温度。

entries.definition: An English-formed doublet of aridity; it exists but is far less common.
entries.definitionCN: 英语自造的 aridity 双重形式；存在但远不常用。

entries.definition: The process of land becoming desert; aridity is the climatic condition, desertification the change.
entries.definitionCN: 土地变成荒漠的过程；aridity 是气候状态，desertification 是变化。

entries.definition: The everyday noun for lacking moisture; aridity is its technical, climate-scale form.
entries.definitionCN: 表示缺水的日常名词；aridity 是其技术化、气候尺度的形式。

entries.definition: A period of unusually low rainfall; aridity is the long-term condition that makes drought hurt.
entries.definitionCN: 一段异常少雨的时期；aridity 是使干旱造成伤害的长期状态。

entries.definition: The removal or loss of water from a body or material; a process, not a climate.
entries.definitionCN: 物体或材料失水的过程；不是气候。

entries.definition: The state of bearing nothing; it may result from aridity but can also come from poor soil or cold.
entries.definitionCN: 不产东西的状态；可能由干旱造成，也可由贫土或寒冷造成。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: arid + -ity: the state of being dry.
normal.cn: arid + -ity：干燥的状态。

normal.en: Latin ariditas is the same word, only with Latin endings.
normal.cn: 拉丁 ariditas 就是同一个词，只换了拉丁词尾。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: aridity index, climatic aridity, aridity gradient.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：干旱指数、气候干旱度、干旱梯度。

normal.en: It is a ratio, not a rainfall total.
normal.cn: 它是一个比值，而不是降水总量。

normal.en: The image is a rain gauge beside an evaporation pan, their readings far apart.
normal.cn: 意象是雨量筒与蒸发皿并立，两个读数相差很远。

abstract.en: Think of a plant that loses more water than it can drink.
abstract.cn: 想象一株植物失去的水多于它能喝到的水。

abstract.en: Think of a voice with no moisture in it at all.
abstract.cn: 想象一个完全不含水分的嗓音。

abstract.en: Think of a field of study where the wells have all run dry.
abstract.cn: 想象一个所有水井都已干涸的研究领域。

examples.en: Aridity in the region has increased by a fifth since 1980.
examples.cn: 该地区的干旱度自 1980 年以来增加了五分之一。

examples.en: The aridity of the air is why the meat dries so fast.
examples.cn: 空气干燥正是肉干得这么快的原因。

examples.en: His aridity made the interview feel like a form to be filled in.
examples.cn: 他的冷淡让采访像在填一张表格。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「arid（干旱）+ ity（性质）」——干旱的性质 → 干旱度

root: 拉丁 arere「干燥」→ aridus「干燥的」→ ariditas「干燥（状态）」→ 英语 aridity。arere 背后的印欧词根属重构，并非有文献的形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses treat aridity first as a climate ratio, then as a soil and habitat condition, then as a quality of writing, feeling and whole disciplines.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项先把 aridity 当作气候比值，再当作土壤与生境状态，最后当作文字、情感与整个学科的性质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gap between what water arrives and what the air can take away.
core.cn: 核心意象：到来的水与空气能带走的水之间的差额。

branches.en: MEASURE: deficit becomes a ratio, and the ratio becomes a zone on a map.
branches.cn: 计量：亏缺变成比值，比值又变成地图上的带。

branches.en: MEDIA: the same shortfall is read in soil, air and the yield of a whole catchment.
branches.cn: 介质：同一种亏缺可在土壤、空气与整个流域的产流中读出。

branches.en: GRADIENT: ecologists line habitats up from moist to extremely dry.
branches.cn: 梯度：生态学者把生境从湿润到极干排成一线。

branches.en: STYLE AND FEELING: writing and manners inherit the same absence of nourishment.
branches.cn: 文风与情感：文字与举止继承了同一种滋养的缺席。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE: a whole field can be judged dry when it stops producing.
branches.cn: 学科：一个领域停止产出时，也可被判为「干」。

intro.en: Aridity is arid plus -ity, the suffix that turns an adjective into a state noun; the Latin equivalent is -itas.
intro.cn: aridity 是 arid 加 -ity，即把形容词变成状态名词的后缀；其拉丁对应是 -itas。

latinIntro.en: Latin ariditas is the direct model: aridus plus -itas, both documented forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ariditas 是直接范本：aridus 加 -itas，两者均有文献。

items.example: An arid basin loses most of its rain to evaporation.
items.exampleCN: 干旱流域的雨大部分被蒸发掉。

items.example: The suffix turns dry into dryness.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「干」变成「干燥」。

items.example: Aridity is mapped by index value.

items.exampleCN: 干旱指数降到 0.2 以下。

items.example: Cover thins along the aridity gradient.
Climatic aridity sets the limit for rain-fed crops.
items.exampleCN: 气候干旱度设定雨养作物的上限。

items.example: Semi-aridity supports grass but not forest.
items.exampleCN: 半干旱状态能长草却长不了森林。

items.example: Hyper-aridity leaves bare rock and salt.
items.exampleCN: 超干旱只留下裸岩与盐。

definition_zh: 贵族；贵族出身的人；（比喻）最佳者、翘楚
definition_en: a member of the highest social class, especially one born into nobility
core_image: 世袭纹章下坐于高位的世家子弟
scene: 宴会厅里烛光摇曳，宾客个个佩着家传徽章。The old aristocrat greeted every guest with courtly grace.
sceneCN: 这里 aristocrat 是「贵族」（第 1 个义项：世袭上层阶级成员）；句意是老贵族以典雅的仪态向每位宾客致意。

collocations.phrase: an aristocrat of the old regime

derivatives.zh: aristocrat 加形容词后缀 -ic，义为「贵族的；气派高雅的」
aristocrat 的抽象名词，义为「贵族阶层；贵族政体」
aristocratic 加 -ally，义为「贵族派头地」
同缀对照词，kratos（民众统治）换成 demos（人民），义为「民主」

senses.title: A member of the nobility
senses.titleCN: 贵族；世袭上层阶级成员
senses.definition: a person born into the highest hereditary social class, holding rank or titles
senses.definitionCN: 出身于最高世袭社会阶层、拥有爵位或头衔的人
senses.example: Hundreds of aristocrats fled France during the Revolution.
senses.exampleCN: 大革命期间数百名贵族逃离法国。
senses.why: The Greek root aristo- means best, and the best-born were the nobles.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根 aristo- 意为「最好的」，出身最显赫者即贵族。

senses.title: A person of aristocratic manner
senses.definition: anyone whose style, manners or tastes suggest the refined elegance of the nobility
senses.definitionCN: 举止品味带有贵族式优雅气派的人，不论出身
senses.example: Though poor, she carried herself like an aristocrat.
senses.exampleCN: 她虽穷，举手投足却像位贵族。
senses.why: The manner is detached from the class and taken as a quality in itself.
senses.whyCN: 气派脱离阶级，本身成为可独立拥有的品质。

senses.title: The finest of its kind
senses.definition: something regarded as the best or most distinguished of its class
senses.definitionCN: 被视为同类中最优秀、最出众的事物
senses.example: This saffron is the aristocrat of all spices.
senses.exampleCN: 这种藏红花是香料中的极品。
senses.why: Aristo- literally means best, so the word returns to its root when ranking things.
senses.whyCN: aristo- 本义即「最好」，比喻义实际上是向词根的回归。

intro.en: Aristocrat comes from Greek aristokrates, a person of the best rule, from aristos and kratos.
intro.cn: aristocrat 源自希腊语 aristokrates，由 aristos（最好的）与 kratos（权力）构成。

items.en: Roots *h2er- (fit together) and *kratos-related stems are reconstructed for best and power.
items.cn: 「最好」与「权力」两词根被分别重构为 *h2er- 及 kratos 相关词干（重构形式）。

items.en: Aristos meant best; kratos meant power or rule; aristokrates named one of the best ruling class.
items.cn: 希腊语 aristos 意为「最好的」，kratos 意为「权力」，aristokrates 指最优统治阶层的一员。

items.en: Aristokratia named government by the best citizens, first a political, not a birth, category.
items.cn: aristokratia 本指「贤良治国」，最初按德才而非血统划分。

items.en: French aristocrate spread in the 18th century, often as a hostile label before the Revolution.
items.cn: 法语 aristocrate 在 18 世纪流行，大革命前常作贬斥标签。

items.en: English borrowed aristocrat in the 1790s in the French political sense.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪 90 年代借入 aristocrat，取其法国政治语境义。

items.en: Today it names nobles by birth and, figuratively, the finest of any class of things.
items.cn: 现代英语既指出身贵族，也比喻各类事物中的极品。

note.en: The family splits into a person (aristocrat), a class (aristocracy) and a style (aristocratic).
note.cn: 词族分工：指人的 aristocrat、指阶层的 aristocracy、指风格的 aristocratic。

entries.definition: the noble class or rule by nobles
entries.definitionCN: 贵族阶层或贵族政体，aristocrat 的同根抽象名词

entries.definition: a ruler with absolute power
entries.definitionCN: 独裁者，同用 -crat（掌权者）后缀但前半不同

entries.definition: an official in a government department
entries.definitionCN: 官僚，同用 -crat 后缀的词族成员

entries.definition: a person of high hereditary rank
entries.definitionCN: 贵族，泛指世袭高位者，是 aristocrat 的近义词

entries.definition: a member of the ancient Roman nobility or any high-born person
entries.definitionCN: （古罗马的）贵族或泛指出身高贵者，与 aristocrat 义近

entries.definition: a Spanish or Portuguese nobleman of the highest rank
entries.definitionCN: （西、葡）最高爵位的显贵，与 aristocrat 义近而语域更窄

normalIntro.en: Break the word into aristos (best) + crat (ruler).
normalIntro.cn: 把词拆成 aristos（最好）加 crat（掌权者）。

normal.en: aristos = best; crat = power: the best who rule.
normal.cn: aristos 意为「最好」，crat 意为「权力」：居上而治的「最优者」。

normal.en: The -crat family: autocrat, bureaucrat, technocrat.
normal.cn: -crat 词族：autocrat、bureaucrat、technocrat。

normal.en: aristocracy is the class; aristocrat is one member.
normal.cn: aristocracy 是阶层，aristocrat 是其中一员。

normal.en: aristocratic describes refined high-class manners.
normal.cn: aristocratic 形容高雅的贵族做派。

normal.en: Figuratively, the aristocrat of tea means the finest tea.
normal.cn: 比喻用法：the aristocrat of tea 即「茶中极品」。

abstract.en: Picture a man with a gold-topped cane inspecting a vineyard he never worked.
abstract.cn: 想象执金柄手杖者巡视自己从未耕作的葡萄园。

abstract.en: Hear the slow, unhurried voice that assumes it will be obeyed.
abstract.cn: 聆听那种理所当然会被人服从的从容语调。

abstract.en: See a family crest carved over a manor gate for three hundred years.
abstract.cn: 想象庄园门楣上刻了三百年的家族纹章。

examples.en: The young aristocrat spent his inheritance on travel and books.
examples.cn: 年轻的贵族把家产花在游历和书籍上。

examples.en: She married an impoverished aristocrat with a grand name.
examples.cn: 她嫁给了一位名头显赫却家道中落的贵族。

examples.en: Connoisseurs rank this vintage as the aristocrat of Burgundies.
examples.cn: 行家们把这款年份酒列为勃艮第酒中的翘楚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱丽事不缺」——贵族小姐爱丽从小仆人环绕，凡事不用自己动手，什么都不缺，真是「爱丽事不缺」。

root: 希腊语 aristos（最好）+ kratos（权力、统治）→ aristokrates（居于权力之最优者）；-crat 后缀同族词有 autocrat、bureaucrat、technocrat。

sensesIntro.en: From born nobles to anyone with lordly manner and figuratively to the finest of a kind.
sensesIntro.cn: 由世袭贵族延伸到有贵族气派者，再比喻为同类中的极品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the best-born sitting at the top of the social ladder
core.cn: 核心意象：出身最优者端坐社会阶梯之顶

branches.en: rank fixed by birth
elegance detached from the class
excellence as modern aristos
branches.cn: 作为现代「最优」义的卓越

branches.en: privilege shown in bearing
the best of a class of things

intro.en: The Greek suffix -crat builds words for power-holders of every kind.
intro.cn: 希腊语后缀 -crat 构成各类掌权者的称谓。

latinIntro.en: The -cracy family names the systems those holders run.
latinIntro.cn: -cracy 词族命名这些掌权者运作的制度。

latinEntries.meaning: one of the best ruling class
